messages:
Alex Chen: CI turned red ~10m ago, ~20 integration tests failing in the kafka-related suites. Logs show repeated Connection refused to localhost:9092. Posting here in eng-infra for quick triage. Anyone else seeing this?

CI Bot: Job https://ci.redwood.ai/job/infra-integration/7423 started by Alex Chen. Status: failed.

Maria Alvarez: repro link? which job number exactly?

Alex Chen: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/infra-integration/7423 (artifacts + raw log attached)

Alex Chen: Relevant snippet from the failure:
```
org.apache.kafka.common.errors.TimeoutException: Failed to update metadata after 60000 ms.
Caused by: java.net.ConnectException: Connection refused ("Connection refused")
 at org.apache.kafka.clients.NetworkClient.poll(NetworkClient.java:...)
```

Jamal Singh: Could be kafka-mock not running or bind failed. Can someone check the CI k8s namespace for the kafka-mock pod status? `kubectl -n ci get pods -l app=kafka-mock`

Alex Chen: I don't have cluster creds from my laptop right now. I ran a local docker compose for the test and kafka-mock came up fine. Odd that only CI is affected.

Nikita (SRE Oncall): I can check. Give me a minute.

Nikita (SRE Oncall): quick status: kafka-mock pod in ci namespace is CrashLoopBackOff on 3 nodes. Init container failed: `bind: address already in use` in the startup script. Looks like a leftover process from yesterday's runs on the node.

Maria Alvarez: ugh. Did the node pool upgrade earlier? I noticed a small infra maintenance window at 02:00 in status page. Could be orphaned processes after restart.

Nikita (SRE Oncall): Yep, there was a rolling upgrade at 02:10. The kafka-mock init script uses `nc -l` for a readiness probe; after upgrade some systemd residuals held the port. I restarted the pods and they now come up cleanly.

Jamal Singh: Nice catch. Can you describe the fix so we don't recur? Sounds like we should avoid relying on ephemeral port bind checks or ensure the container retries.

Nikita (SRE Oncall): Short-term: restarted the kafka-mock daemonset pods and cleared the leftover process on the nodes (killed orphaned `nc` instances). Long-term: we should add a proper healthcheck + containerized wait logic instead of using host-level netcat and make the init container retry/backoff. I'll open an infra ticket.

Alex Chen: Reran the CI job immediately after you restarted?

Nikita (SRE Oncall): I manually retriggered the failing job 7423 (re-run full pipeline).

CI Bot: Job https://ci.redwood.ai/job/infra-integration/7423 (re-run) started.

CI Bot: Job https://ci.redwood.ai/job/infra-integration/7423 (re-run) SUCCESS. All tests passed.

Maria Alvarez: Phew. For sanity, can someone add a quick smoke test that fails fast when kafka-mock isn't reachable, so devs see clearer error messaging instead of dozens of timeout stack traces?

Jamal Singh: Agreed. I'll add a small preflight that checks the service endpoint and fails quickly with a readable message. Also will add an environment var to skip kafka e2e on PRs that opt out: `CI_SKIP_KAFKA=true` to speed local dev debug.

Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. Can we track the infra follow-up in a ticket? Nikita, if you create one, tag it `infra/ci` and assign to Jamal for the CI image change and to SRE for the daemonset healthcheck work.

Nikita (SRE Oncall): Done — https://issues.redwood.ai/infra/CI-314 created. Description: "kafka-mock daemonset: add containerized healthcheck and retry logic; avoid host netcat usage; ensure restart-safe on node upgrades" — assigned to Jamal + SRE.

Alex Chen: Closing this thread — since rerun passed, I'll unskip the PRs blocked by 7423. Thanks :thumbsup:

Maria Alvarez: Thanks all :party_parrot:
